title: Subtracting with regrouping: 52 − 17
examples: What does borrowing mean in subtraction?
How do I do 52 take away 17?

explain.say: Priya has 52 stickers and gives 17 to her friend. How many are left? Look at the blocks: 52 is 5 rods and 2 cubes, and we must take away 17. Let us see what goes wrong, and how to fix it. You will get 35.
Start with the ones. We must take away 7 ones, but look: there are only 2 cubes in 52. You cannot take 7 from 2! Do you have an idea where to get more ones?
Here is the trick. Break one rod into 10 ones. Now there are 4 tens and 12 ones. 12 take away 7 leaves 5. See the 5 cubes left? Breaking a ten like this is called regrouping, or borrowing.
Now the tens. There are 4 rods, that is 40, and we take away 1 ten, that is 10. 40 take away 10 leaves 30. So what is 30 and 5?
It is 35! Fantastic. So 52 take away 17 equals 35. You can check by adding back: 35 plus 17 makes 52. Challenge: try 63 take away 28, then check by adding.

faq.q: What does borrowing mean in subtraction?
faq.a: Borrowing means taking one ten from the tens column and breaking it into 10 ones. It is also called regrouping or exchanging.
You cannot take 7 things away if you only have 2. So you regroup: break a ten to get 12 ones, and 12 take away 7 is 5.
asks: What do I do when the top digit is smaller?

faq.q: How do I do 52 take away 17?
faq.a: Break a ten, so 52 becomes 4 tens and 12 ones. 12 minus 7 is 5, and 4 tens minus 1 ten is 3 tens. The answer is 35.

faq.q: How do I check a subtraction?
faq.a: Add your answer to the number you took away. If you get the starting number, you are right: 35 plus 17 is 52.
asks: How can I check my answer?

faq.a: No. 5 tens and 2 ones is 52, and 4 tens and 12 ones is still 52. Only the packing changes.

facts: Breaking 1 ten into 10 ones does not change the value of a number.

quiz.why: Regroup: 13 minus 8 is 5, and 3 tens minus 1 ten is 2 tens. So 25.

wrong.0: 35 comes from doing 8 minus 3 instead of regrouping.
wrong.2: 24 is one short: 13 minus 8 is 5, not 4.
